title: Move the decimal with the unit
hook: 125 cents is not €12.50. The unit tells you the conversion factor.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert cents to euros using the stated unit relationship.

misconception: Converting cents to euros requires moving the decimal only one place.
objective: Convert cents to euros using the stated unit relationship.

claims.text: A euro contains 100 cents. A divides cents by 100; B deliberately divides by ten instead. Scaled model; unit arithmetic; 100 cents/€; B deliberately wrong.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Cents=125c, A=€1.25 and B=€12.5. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",100]; B=["/","x",10]; x denotes Cents. At x=125, A=1.25, B=12.5; recall at x=140: B=14. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: The denominator comes from the unit definition: one hundred cents per euro. Dividing by ten changes the amount by the wrong factor. Carry the unit alongside the digits so the decimal movement has a reason.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",100]; B=["/","x",10]; x denotes Cents. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A euro contains 100 cents. A divides cents by 100; B deliberately divides by ten instead. Change only Cents to 140c. What is B (Tenths) now? Correct: €14. Use B's stated rule with Cents=140c: it gives €14. The denominator comes from the unit definition: one hundred cents per euro. Dividing by ten changes the amount by the wrong factor. Carry the unit alongside the digits so the decimal movement has a reason.

recall.question: A euro contains 100 cents. A divides cents by 100; B deliberately divides by ten instead. Change only Cents to 140c. What is B (Tenths) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Cents=140c: it gives €14. The denominator comes from the unit definition: one hundred cents per euro. Dividing by ten changes the amount by the wrong factor. Carry the unit alongside the digits so the decimal movement has a reason.
